26.questionText: Дополнительный материал к заданию: Your amazing brain Your brain controls everything you do. It makes it possible for you to think, learn, create and feel emotions, to blink and breathe and for your heart to beat. It is so amazing that a famous scientist once called it “the most complex thing we have yet discovered in our universe”. Trying to make sense of the brain isn’t easy. We know it’s the organ that makes us human by giving us the ability to create art and language, make decisions and produce rational thought. It’s also responsible for our personalities, memories, movements and how we understand the world. Can this small grey organ, which weighs less than one and a half kilos, really do so much? Amazingly, your brain contains 100 billion microscopic cells called neurons – it would take you 3,000 years to count them all. Whenever you dream, laugh, think, see or move, it’s because signals are racing between these neurons. Believe it or not, the activity in your brain never stops. Your neurons create and send more messages than all the phones in the world. And also one neuron creates only a very small amount of electricity, all your neurons together can produce enough electricity to power a light bulb. So exactly how fast does your brain work? Well, imagine this: a bee lands on your foot. Neurons in your skin send this information to your brain at a speed of more than 240 kilometres per hour. Your brain then uses other neurons to send the message back to your foot to shake the bee off quickly. These neurons can send this information at more than 320 kilometres per hour. No computer has your brain’s increadible ability to cope with the amount of information coming from your eyes, ears and other sensory organs. How does your brain allow you to learn things that you will use in the future? The structure of your brain changes every time you have a new thought, remember or learn something. For example, riding a bike seems impossible at first, but soon you are able to do it. As you practice, your brain sends ‘bike riding’ messages again and again. Soon, the actions are learnt and you’re able to ride a bike easily from then on. The human brain in the text is compared to… .

86.questionText: Дополнительный материал к заданию: Cheating in Sports Cheating in sports is widely condemned, yet the line between fair play and gamesmanship can be blurry. A notable example of cheating occurred when Spain fielded non-disabled athletes in the 2000 Sydney Paralympics basketball team. In contrast, gamesmanship involves bending the rules to gain an advantage without outright cheating. A case of gamesmanship is British cyclist Philip Hindes, who intentionally crashed his bike during the 2012 Olympics to restart a race after a bad start. His team ultimately won gold. Other tactics include faking injuries or wasting time to disrupt opponents, as seen with badminton player Carolina Marins at the 2016 Rio Olympics, who screamed to distract her rival but did not break any rules. Referees play a crucial role in identifying cheating, but they can miss important incidents. In cricket, batters often stay on the field after being hit by the ball, despite knowing they should leave. This behavior is not considered cheating. Diego Maradona’s infamous "Hand of God" goal in the 1986 World Cup is a clear example of cheating; he scored using his hand, and the referee missed it. Conversely, Brazilian player Rivaldo faked an injury in the 2002 World Cup and was fined when caught. Sometimes players might even lose on purpose for strategic advantages, as demonstrated by four badminton doubles teams at the 2012 London Olympics, which were disqualified for poor sportsmanship despite breaking no rules. In conclusion, while bending the rules may add intrigue to sports competitions, it raises questions about fairness and integrity. What is an example of cheating mentioned in the text?

answers.text: A badminton player distracted the competitor.

A package of things useful to give first aid is called a first aid kit. Lives can be saved even without a first aid kit. What is required is basic knowledge. First aid can be done just about anywhere. In places far from hospitals, first aid may be the only help possible until the person can be taken to a hospital or clinic.
